memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing, and Moses and Aaron and his sons used it to wash their hands and feet. They washed whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 40:30-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"They washed whenever they entered." Not once at ordination. Every time.

These were consecrated priests, already anointed, already clothed in sacred garments. And still they washed — hands and feet, again and again, throughout their service.

Hands and feet are what get dirty in daily work. You do not walk through a camp and come back clean.

Jesus made precisely this distinction. When Peter asked Him to wash more than his feet, Jesus replied that a person who has had a bath needs only to wash their feet; their whole body is clean (John 13:10).

That is a wonderfully freeing picture. Our standing before God is settled — we have been bathed, justified once and for all (Rom 5:1). But walking through the world dirties our feet, and we need regular cleansing.

Confession is not re-earning salvation. It is washing your feet. If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us and purify us (1 John 1:9).

Some Christians live in constant doubt, washing as though the bath never happened. Others stop washing altogether and wonder why fellowship feels distant.

Bathed once. Feet washed daily. Both.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you confess your sins regularly or avoid facing them?
2. Have you confused confession with re-earning God's acceptance?
3. What has dirtied your feet this week that needs bringing to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that I am fully cleansed in Christ. Wash my feet today, and keep my walk with You clear. Amen.
